question: Which entry sets an arbitrary local style property on 3.1.28, and which property ids does the style-name table assign to the properties a native-looking Manager needs?
prototype_hypothesis: int32_t lv_obj_set_local_style_prop(lv_obj_t *obj, uint32_t property, lv_style_value_t value, uint32_t selector); the low byte of a style-table id is the property, the byte above it is the value type (1 int, 2 colour, 3 pointer).
callsite_evidence: sub_C2BCCDC is `return sub_C2BC984(a1, 0x1D, a2, a3)` and the desktop list builder calls it with 255 as a bg_opa.

The style-name table (pairs of name pointer and id) at 0xc726a40 maps radius to 0x10c, bg_color to 0x21c, bg_opa to 0x11d, pad_top..pad_right to 0x110..0x113, pad_row to 0x114, border_width to 0x130, text_color to 0x258, text_font to 0x35a, clip_corner to 0x12d.
control_flow_evidence: Every lv_obj_set_style_* wrapper tail-calls 0xc2bc984, so it is the single local-style writer.
ownership_analysis: The style value is stored by value in the object's local style; a font pointer stays owned by the font manager, colours and integers are copied.
unsafe_assumptions: A colour value is passed as 0x00RRGGBB in r2; this is checked on the emulator only.
recommended_probe: Set radius, bg_opa and text_color on a Manager row and compare the rendered frame with the stock Settings page.
